newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures end lower in all months.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures end lower in all months.

text.p: All Tokyo gold futures closed lower on Thursday, weighed down by selling from individual investors who were discouraged by the weaker New York market overnight, traders said.
TOCOM gold futures were six to 14 yen lower, with most-active December ending 11 yen lower at 1,314 yen per gram.
Spot gold was quoted at $353.20/353.50 per ounce at 0713 GMT, up from $352.25/352.75 in New York on Wednesday.
"All months fell from the opening on selling from local investors. But in the near term, the distant December contract is expected to find support around 1,310 yen," a trader said.

The steep falls in the Tokyo stock market since last week could be a bearish factor for the Tokyo precious metal markets, since many individual investors use stocks as collateral for building positions, traders said.
"Active long liquidation from Japanese investors may emerge if the Tokyo stock market falls further," a brokerage house trader said.
Platinum futures closed weaker in all months, in line with gold. Prices were four to six yen lower, with the benchmark December 1997 contract down four yen at 1,336 yen per gram.

Traders said they had received no official notice yet from the Russian platinum group metal export agency on negotiations for 1997 supply contracts with Japan. The talks have been delayed since mid-December.
"We're still waiting for confirmation on the schedule of the negotiations," a source at a major trade house said.
Palladium futures ended mostly firmer, with benchmark December up four yen at 451 yen per gram. December silver futures were unchanged at 177.7 yen per 10 grams.
